inputs.subset_rule: every 5-th file (sorted path order, files 0, 5, 10, ...) of each of the Run2016G and Run2016H SingleMuon listings; all MC files
inputs.reason: speed: the validation is a test of the skill, a run-representative subset is enough for a few per mille statistics

luminosity.source: Open Data record 1059 pp_2016lumibyls.csv, 'recorded' column, summed over the lumi sections present in the processed files and in the golden JSON (record 14220)

pairs.definition: pairs (each muon once as tag; tag pT>29 GeV tight+iso+trigger-matched; event fired IsoMu24 or IsoTkMu24; 70<m<115 GeV; probe a tracker muon)

bins.label: eta0.0-0.9_pt30-40
bins.note: Accepted open issue. |pull| > 5 in a high-statistics bin where the POG uncertainty is only 0.02-0.1 percent: our SF is 0.2-0.5 percent above the POG in the 30-50 GeV bins of this working point (confirmed by a fit-free counting cross-check in the ARC review). Not covered by our uncertainties: MC-template statistics (MC/data pairs = 0.44; the tight-ID test shows such an offset shrinks with MC statistics, not tested for isolation) and the run-mix difference to the POG (F late + G + H). Fits converge and the background, window and tag systematics are below 0.1 percent here.

bins.label: eta0.0-0.9_pt26-30
bins.note: Accepted open issue, cause not found. The IsoMu24 SF is 0.8-1.5 percent above the POG in the high-statistics bins (weighted SF/POG 1.013 at 30-60 GeV). It is robust against the fit, mass window, background shape, pileup weights, tag pT, the run era (G vs H differ by 0.14 percent) and the event-level HLT requirement (skill / no HLT / path-specific). It depends on the probe pass definition: with bit 2 (Iso) alone instead of bit 2 or bit 8 the SF/POG at 40-50 GeV is 1.000-1.001 for |eta| > 0.9 and 1.012 in the barrel (weighted 30-60 GeV: 1.008); bit 8 alone gives SF/POG 0.963-0.986. That is a lead, not a proof: the tag match stays the OR of bits 2|8 in the skim and cannot be changed offline, and the POG probe definition is not known. The object pT threshold changes the efficiencies strongly below 30 GeV (data 0.876 at >=24 vs 0.709 at >=27 GeV, 26-30 GeV bin) but the SF only by <= 0.9 percent; the scan at 40-50 GeV is vacuous. Event-level filter-bit bias is negligible (4.6e-5 of matched probes).

lumi_note: POG muon_Z.json.gz covers 2016F(late)+G+H; the data here are G+H only (see run_dependence for the era split)
